newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end quiet day higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end quiet day higher.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended higher on Monday on light buying from local investors but prices were confined to a narrow range throughout the day, traders said.
Prices for the September 1997 to May 1998 contract ranged from 20 to 100 yen per tonne higher.
The newly-listed July 1998 contract closed at 14,690 yen per tonne, down 10 yen from the opening.
The day's estimated trade volume was 41,426 lots.
The yen's weaker tendency against the dollar supported all contracts during the morning session, but the market lacked factors to stimulate active trade, traders said.
Local investors are waiting for the weather market to start, they said.
Open interest in Tokyo corn futures fell to 420,915 lots as of June 13 from 444,351 lots as of May 13, the Tokyo Grain Exchange said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.70-1/2 per bushel at 0730 GMT, against $2.71-1/2 at Friday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.48-1/2 a bushel at 0730 GMT, down from $8.54-1/2 at Friday's close.
